title: A User’s Guide to Mail-In Voting

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》旗下每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 我们将于 11 月在 nytimes.com 上直播精选的采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是一份日报。

sentences.en: An unprecedented number of Americans are about to do it, despite the president's attempts to cast doubt on it.
sentences.zh: 尽管总统千方百计对此表示怀疑，但史无前例数量的美国人即将参与其中。

sentences.en: Today, a guide to voting by mail.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将为您带来邮寄投票指南。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Luke Broadwater, about the rules and realities of the process across the country.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事卢克·布罗德沃特探讨了全国各地这项程序的规则与现实情况。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是 10 月 1 日，星期四。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: Are you recording?
sentences.zh: 你在录音吗？

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 我是。

sentences.en: Did you put on a suit for us?
sentences.zh: 你专门为我们穿了西装吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm at the Senate.
sentences.zh: 没有，我在参议院。

sentences.en: So I'm up here with you guys in the phone booth.
sentences.zh: 所以我跟你们一起挤在电话亭里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: Because in reality, you cover Congress, even though for our purposes, you have become the kind of pop-up mail-in voting reporter.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，你负责国会报道，尽管为了我们的节目，你已经变成了一种“快闪式”邮寄投票记者。

sentences.en: Well, I got stuck with the Postal Service and that sort of led into this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我被指派负责邮政服务，这差不多就引出了这个话题。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: It's like an important story and we got to make sure that the mail-in voting is running correctly.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个重要的新闻，我们必须确保邮寄投票能够正常进行。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: So.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: It's probably the most important temporary beat I can remember in my time at the Times.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我在《时报》工作期间经历过的最重要的临时专责报道。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: Agreed.

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: So, Luke, we want to talk to you about the mechanics of voting right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，卢克，我们想和你聊聊目前投票的具体机制。

sentences.en: Literally the most news-you-can-use information I think we've ever covered on the daily.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是我认为我们在《The Daily》节目中报道过的最具实用价值的信息。

sentences.en: And my sense is that there are three ways to vote right now.
sentences.zh: 我的理解是，目前有三种投票方式。

sentences.en: In person on election day, in person before election day through early voting, or by mail.
sentences.zh: 选举日当天亲自投票、选举日之前通过提前投票亲自投票，或者通过邮寄投票。

sentences.en: And I want to focus on that third one, voting by mail, because it feels like more Americans are going to be doing that this election year than ever before.
sentences.zh: 我想把重点放在第三种，即邮寄投票上，因为今年大选选择这种方式的美国人似乎比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: So let's just start with a very basic question, which is how do you, how do all of us go about voting by mail?
sentences.zh: 那我们就从一个非常基础的问题开始，也就是你、我们所有人究竟该如何进行邮寄投票？

sentences.en: Well, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得对。

sentences.en: We're doing an election in a whole new way.
sentences.zh: 我们正在以一种全新方式进行选举。

sentences.en: More than a million Americans have already voted.
sentences.zh: 已经有超过一百万美国人投了票。

sentences.en: I mean, that number's rising by the day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个数字每天都在增长。

sentences.en: But the first thing you need to know about voting by mail is you have to register to vote.
sentences.zh: 但关于邮寄投票，你需要知道的第一件事就是你必须先进行选民登记。

sentences.en: And there are states where you can register to vote on election day.
sentences.zh: 有些州允许你在选举日当天进行登记。

sentences.en: But if you want to vote by mail, you've pretty much got to do that right now.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想邮寄投票，你基本上现在就得去办。

sentences.en: Most states require you to register to vote by mail by early October.
sentences.zh: 大多数州要求你在 10 月上旬之前完成邮寄投票的登记。

sentences.en: Then after that, there are sort of two categories of states.
sentences.zh: 然后在此之后，各州大致分为两类。

sentences.en: There are states that, once you're registered, will automatically mail you a ballot.
sentences.zh: 有一类州，一旦你登记了，就会自动给你寄送选票。

sentences.en: That's what people call universal mail-in voting.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们所说的全民邮寄投票。

sentences.en: And there are states, the majority of states, where you have to actively apply to get that mail-in ballot.
sentences.zh: 还有另一类州——占大多数的州——你必须主动申请才能获得邮寄选票。

sentences.en: So let's start with the first category, states that automatically mail registered voters a ballot.
sentences.zh: 那我们先从第一类开始，即自动向已登记选民寄送选票的州。

sentences.en: Which states are those?
sentences.zh: 有哪些州属于这一类？

sentences.en: Well, there are nine states and the District of Columbia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有九个州和哥伦比亚特区。

sentences.en: They are Washington, Oregon, California,
sentences.zh: 它们是华盛顿州、俄勒冈州、加利福尼亚州、

sentences.en: Utah, Nevada, Colorado, Hawaii, New Jersey, and Vermont.
sentences.zh: 犹他州、内华达州、科罗拉多州、夏威夷州、新泽西州和佛蒙特州。

sentences.en: I guess we should warn listeners, this may be the kind of episode where you literally hear all 50 states named, and that's just the way it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该提醒听众，这可能是一期你会听到所有 50 个州的名字被逐一念出的节目，事实就是这样。

sentences.en: We seek to inform.
sentences.zh: 我们致力于提供资讯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: So in those nine states, what exactly happens?
sentences.zh: 那么在那九个州里，具体会发生什么？

sentences.en: So if it works according to plan, every single person who has registered to vote will receive a mail-in ballot at their house.
sentences.zh: 如果按计划进行，每一个登记投票的人都会在家中收到一张邮寄选票。

sentences.en: That is the same thing as an absentee ballot.
sentences.zh: 这和缺席选票是一回事。

sentences.en: It's no different, but it's sent to you automatically.
sentences.zh: 没有任何区别，但它是自动寄给你的。

sentences.en: So all you have to do is receive it, fill it out, and mail it in.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要收到它、填好，然后寄回去就行了。

sentences.en: And what is the second category of states when it comes to mail-in voting?
sentences.zh: 那么在邮寄投票方面，第二类州是怎样的？

sentences.en: So in all other states, they require you to request for an absentee ballot to actually get it and then vote.
sentences.zh: 所以在所有其他州，他们要求你申请缺席选票才能真正获得它并进行投票。

sentences.en: In some of those states, like Maryland and Wisconsin and Iowa and Illinois and Ohio,
sentences.zh: 在其中一些州，比如马里兰州、威斯康星州、爱荷华州、伊利诺伊州和俄亥俄州，

sentences.en: they will automatically send you an application that you have to fill out to get the mail-in ballot.
sentences.zh: 他们会自动向你发送一份申请表，你必须填写该表格才能获得邮寄选票。

sentences.en: But in all other states, you have to go online, fill out a form proactively to get the ballot sent to you.
sentences.zh: 但在所有其他州，你必须上网，主动填写表格才能把选票寄给你。

sentences.en: And those include some of the most important states in the election, including Pennsylvania and
sentences.zh: 其中包括选举中一些最重要的州，包括宾夕法尼亚州和

sentences.en: Florida.
sentences.zh: Florida.

sentences.en: So let's say you have this ballot application in front of you.
sentences.zh: 假设你面前就放着这张选票申请表。

sentences.en: What then?
sentences.zh: 那又怎样？

sentences.en: What does it entail?
sentences.zh: 它包含哪些内容？

sentences.en: So in the majority of states in the country, you're going to be able to simply request a mail-in ballot because of the coronavirus pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以在全国大多数州，由于冠状病毒大流行，你将能够非常轻松地申请邮寄选票。

sentences.en: But there are still five states in the country, mostly in the
sentences.zh: 但全国仍有五个州，主要在

sentences.en: South, Indiana, Tennessee, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Texas require a excuse beyond the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 南部——印第安纳州、田纳西州、密西西比州、路易斯安那州和德克萨斯州——要求提供大流行之外的正当理由。

sentences.en: Those are the states where it's going to be harder to vote by mail because they require an additional excuse beyond simply surviving like we all are in this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 在这些州，邮寄投票会更加困难，因为除了像我们所有人一样在这场大流行中艰难求生之外，它们还需要额外的理由。

sentences.en: So everything you just described covers all 50 states, which in one form or another, whether it's
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才描述的涵盖了所有 50 个州，无论形式如何，无论是

sentences.en: super easy or a little hard or quite restrictive, all allow for mail-in voting for this election.
sentences.zh: 超级简单、有点困难还是相当严格，所有这些州在这场选举中都允许邮寄投票。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.en: So let's talk about the timing for sending in a ballot application.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈寄送选票申请的时间安排。

sentences.en: When do you need to request a ballot by?
sentences.zh: 你必须在什么时候之前申请选票？

sentences.en: Well, each state is different and has different rules.
sentences.zh: 嗯，每个州的情况都不同，规则也各异。

sentences.en: Some of them require you to request a ballot as much as two weeks or even three weeks before the election.
sentences.zh: 其中一些州要求你在选举前两周甚至三周就申请选票。

sentences.en: In Indiana, it's 12 days before the election.
sentences.zh: 在印第安纳州，是选举前 12 天。

sentences.en: In Virginia, it's 11 days.
sentences.zh: 在弗吉尼亚州，是 11 天。

sentences.en: In Missouri, it's 13 days.
sentences.zh: 在密苏里州，是 13 天。

sentences.en: Some states will allow you to request a mail-in ballot in the days before the election.
sentences.zh: 有些州允许你在选举前的几天内申请邮寄选票。

sentences.en: For instance,
sentences.zh: 比如，

sentences.en: Ohio will allow you to request a mail-in ballot just two days before the election.
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州允许你在选举前仅仅两天申请邮寄选票。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: Hmm.

sentences.en: Okay, so let's say you do this all.
sentences.zh: 好吧，假设你把这些都做完了。

sentences.en: You fill out a ballot application.
sentences.zh: 你填好了选票申请表。

sentences.en: It arrives.
sentences.zh: 它送到了。

sentences.en: A ballot is sent to your home in response.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，一张选票会被寄到你家。

sentences.en: Let's talk about what happens to that ballot, what a person needs to do to successfully fill it out.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈那张选票会怎么样，一个人需要做什么才能成功填好它。

sentences.en: Because my sense is that it's not entirely straightforward.
sentences.zh: 因为我的感觉是，这个过程并非完全直截了当。

sentences.en: Well, each state is different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，每个州的情况都不同。

sentences.en: But in many of the states, it's a rather simple process.
sentences.zh: 但在许多州，这是一个相当简单的过程。

sentences.en: You simply fill in the bubble.
sentences.zh: 你只需涂黑圆圈。

sentences.en: You seal your envelope with the ballot inside.
sentences.zh: 把选票装进信封并封好。

sentences.en: The envelope has the postage paid for it already and you mail it in or you take it to a secure drop box.
sentences.zh: 信封上的邮资已经付过了，你可以把它寄出去，或者送到安全的投票投递箱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: But there are a number of states that require several forms of identification or hoops to jump through in order for you to have your ballot count.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些州要求提供多种形式的身份证明，或者设置重重关卡，你的选票才能被计入。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: In some states like Pennsylvania, there is a secrecy envelope you have to place your ballot into.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州等一些州，你必须把选票放入一个保密信封中。

sentences.en: What is a secrecy envelope?
sentences.zh: 什么是保密信封？

sentences.en: Well, in some ways, it's a relic from the past, but it's an extra envelope inside the envelope.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某种程度上，它是过去的遗物，但它是信封内部的额外一个信封。

sentences.en: And so you have to put the ballot in this to keep it secret.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须把选票放进这个信封里以保持保密。

sentences.en: So when someone opens it, they have to open another envelope firSt. But if you don't use that envelope within an envelope, your vote might not count.
sentences.zh: 因此，当别人打开它时，他们必须先打开另一个信封。但如果你没有在信封里使用这个小信封，你的选票可能就不会被计入。

sentences.en: And more than 100,000 votes could be in jeopardy because of it.
sentences.zh: 因此可能会有超过 10 万张选票陷入危险之中。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: Wow.

sentences.en: And then there's some states that really make it an intereSt. Like Alabama, for instance, requires a copy of your ID and then you need two witnesses older than 18
sentences.zh: 然后有些州真的让事情变得很有趣。比如阿拉巴马州，要求提供你的身份证复印件，然后你需要两个 18 岁以上的见证人

sentences.en: to sign the envelope affirming that you are who you say you are.
sentences.zh: 在信封上签字，证明你确实是你所说的那个人。

sentences.en: So you've not.
sentences.zh: 所以你没有。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: Wow.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: So or they will accept a notary public.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会接受公证员的签字。

sentences.en: And so especially in the South, we see a lot of requirements still for identifications and for witness signatures, which can make it much more onerous to vote by mail.
sentences.zh: 因此，特别是在南部，我们看到对身份证明和见证人签字仍然有很多要求，这会使得邮寄投票变得繁琐得多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: It sounds like in some ways, the mail-in voting is significantly harder than in-person voting in those states.
sentences.zh: 听起来在某些方面，在这些州里，邮寄投票比亲自投票要困难得多。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: So as we move along in the chain of custody of a ballot, once you have filled out this ballot,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们沿着选票的保管链继续前进时，一旦你填好了这张选票，

sentences.en: according to these quirky rules of various states, and you put your ballot in the mail,
sentences.zh: 并根据各州这些古怪的规则把选票投入邮筒，

sentences.en: I've always wanted to ask somebody this question.
sentences.zh: 我一直想问某人这个问题。

sentences.en: What happens to a mail-in ballot once it arrives at the board of election?
sentences.zh: 邮寄选票到达选举委员会后会发生什么？

sentences.en: Does it get opened right away?
sentences.zh: 它们会立即被打开吗？

sentences.en: Does it go into a giant pile to be opened later?
sentences.zh: 它们会堆成巨型堆等待以后打开吗？

sentences.en: What exactly happens to it?
sentences.zh: 它到底会经历什么？

sentences.en: Well, again, every state is different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，同样，每个州的情况都不同。

sentences.en: They all will go into piles.
sentences.zh: 它们都会被堆成堆。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Some have internal procedures where they, because of concern over the coronavirus, will let them sit untouched for 24 hours before touching them.
sentences.zh: 由于对冠状病毒的担忧，一些州有内部程序，允许选票在不被触碰的情况下静置 24 小时。

sentences.en: But after that, each state has its own regulations about when election officials can start to handle the ballots.
sentences.zh: 但在那之后，每个州都有关于选举官员何时可以开始处理选票的各自规定。

sentences.en: For instance, in Arizona, you can start tallying the mail-in ballots 14 days before the election.
sentences.zh: 例如，在亚利桑那州，你可以在选举前 14 天开始清点邮寄选票。

sentences.en: Those go into sort of a secure system that is not released publicly until the polls close on election day.
sentences.zh: 这些选票会进入一种安全系统，在选举日投票站关闭之前不会向公众公布。

sentences.en: In Colorado, they start counting
sentences.zh: 在科罗拉多州，他们开始计票的时间是

sentences.en: 15 days before the election.
sentences.zh: 选举前 15 天。

sentences.en: In Florida, it's actually 22 days before the election.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达州，实际上是选举前 22 天。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: Wow.

sentences.en: But for better or worse, there are eight states, including the battleground states of Pennsylvania
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，有八个州，包括宾夕法尼亚州和密歇根州这两个关键摇摆州，

sentences.en: and Michigan, that will not allow election officials to start counting the mail-in ballots until election day.
sentences.zh: 不允许选举官员在选举日之前开始清点邮寄选票。

sentences.en: Now, all of that is subject to change because there are more than 300 lawsuits currently throughout the country of people fighting over these rules.
sentences.zh: 现在，所有这些都可能会改变，因为目前全国各地有 300 多起诉讼，人们正在为这些规则争论不休。

sentences.en: And I only expect that to continue and grow in volume after the election.
sentences.zh: 我预计这种情况在选举后只会继续下去，并且规模会进一步扩大。

sentences.en: And is it the case that all of these lawsuits are challenging existing rules?
sentences.zh: 难道所有这些诉讼都是在对现行规则提出挑战吗？

sentences.en: People are now saying, hey, wait a minute, with mail-in voting being as significant as it is, we don't like these rules anymore?

sentences.en: But because of the president's rhetoric around mail-in voting being fraudulent, and because of different levels of concern around the coronavirus, what we're seeing this year is
sentences.zh: 但由于总统关于邮寄投票存在欺诈的言论，以及对冠状病毒的不同担忧程度，我们今年看到的情况是

sentences.zh: 民主党人以远超共和党人的数量进行邮寄投票。

sentences.en: And so what you have is a partisan breakdown over mail-in voting to a large extent.

sentences.en: And that's why we're seeing a lot of the interested parties react the way they are in terms of these lawsuits.

sentences.en: But, you know, there are lawsuits in 44 states right now, and there's more than 300 of them.

sentences.en: So it's literally being contested step by step this entire election.
sentences.zh: 所以这场选举的每一步实际上都在面临法律抗争。

sentences.en: So you're saying as complicated as everything you have just described already is, it's still

sentences.en: So, Luke, as you said, we have never done this before.

sentences.zh: 主要基于选举日当天的投票。

sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: It is done.
sentences.zh: 尘埃落定。

sentences.zh: 对于这次选举，情况将大不相同，特别是在那些直到选举日才开始拆封邮寄选票的州。

sentences.en: Remember, those are eight states, including some of the battleground states.

sentences.en: And so in those states, what you could see is a phenomenon that some analysts are calling the red mirage.
sentences.zh: 所以在这些州，你可能会看到一种被一些分析人士称为“红色海市蜃楼”的现象。

sentences.en: And what is that?

sentences.en: The red mirage is the idea that because of the partisan divide on mail-in voting, on election day, you will see largely Republicans voting in person.
sentences.zh: 红色海市蜃楼是指这样一种观点：由于在邮寄投票问题上的党派分歧，在选举日当天，你会看到主要是共和党人在亲自投票。

sentences.en: And so it may look in some of these closed states that Donald Trump is winning election day and is up
sentences.zh: 因此在其中一些提前关闭的州，看起来可能会像是唐纳德·特朗普赢得了选举日投票并处于领先地位，

sentences.zh: 并且正在走向胜利，而实际上还有海量的民主党邮寄选票尚未被统计，在接下来的一两天内也不会被统计。

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.en: So it's a red mirage because it will be a temporary portrait of a Trump-like victory based on the absence of mail-in ballots being fully counted.

sentences.en: That's exactly right.

sentences.en: And this year, based on the trends we're seeing so far, because it's mostly Democrats, again, in some states, two to one, three to one, who are requesting the mail-in ballots,

sentences.en: that it's going to be the Democratic vote that is waiting in the mail, so to speak, to come in in the days after the election.
sentences.zh: 因此民主党的选票将“滞留在邮件中”，可以说是等待在选举结束后的几天内陆续到达。

sentences.en: And how long, Luke, might a red mirage-like situation exist?

sentences.en: Which I guess is another way of saying precisely how long will it take for all these mail-in ballots to be counted in some of these states?
sentences.zh: 我想这也是在问，在其中一些州，所有这些邮寄选票到底需要花多长时间才能清点完毕？

sentences.en: Well, again, each state is different, as we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们讨论过的，每个州的情况都不一样。

sentences.en: But really, honestly, it depends on how big the leads are.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，这确实取决于领先优势有多大。

sentences.en: So if Trump is up by a little bit, let's say, in Pennsylvania on Election Day and Biden overtakes him the next day, well, then you know, because it's very unlikely that there's
sentences.zh: 因此，比方说，如果特朗普在选举日当天在宾夕法尼亚州略微领先，而拜登在第二天反超，那么你就会知道，因为不太可能有

sentences.en: a ton of Republican mail-in ballots waiting around.

sentences.en: But the bigger Trump's lead and the larger amount of mail-in ballots yet to be counted, you know, it could take a week or maybe more.

sentences.zh: 卢克，我想象一下在选举之夜，某个特定州会有什么样的感受。

sentences.en: And so let's look at a place like Ohio.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看像俄亥俄州这样的地方。

sentences.en: Do we imagine that a state like that is going to report to the networks, for example, to the New York Times, to the Associated Press?
sentences.zh: 我们是否可以设想，这样一个州会向各大电视网、比如《纽约时报》、美联社报告说：

sentences.en: And we need X number of days to count it.

sentences.en: So just like, please stand by and be patient.
sentences.zh: 所以请大家稍安勿躁，保持耐心。

sentences.en: And we'll get back to you.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会再向大家汇报。

sentences.en: So I would say that Ohio will be in a better shape than some other states because they're allowing the mail-in ballots to be counted ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说的是，俄亥俄州的情况会比其他一些州好一些，因为他们允许提前清点邮寄选票。

sentences.en: So I think in Ohio, you may have a case where you have a sizable portion of the mail-in vote counted in those early returns of Election Day.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为在俄亥俄州，你可能会发现在选举日的早期计票结果中，已经统计了相当大比例的邮寄选票。

sentences.en: Now, Ohio is allowing ballots to be counted that are postmarked by the Election Day for
sentences.zh: 现在，俄亥俄州允许清点在选举日或之前加盖邮戳、并在选举日后

sentences.en: 11 days afterwards.
sentences.zh: 11天内送达的选票。

sentences.en: But again, because they're allowed to count early, we may see Ohio in a better shape than
sentences.zh: 但同样，因为他们被允许提前计票，在选举之夜，我们看到俄亥俄州的情况可能会好于

sentences.en: Pennsylvania or Michigan on election night.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州或密歇根州。

sentences.en: And so what will this look like if you know in Pennsylvania or in Michigan then?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你在宾夕法尼亚州或密歇根州，情况又会是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: So those are the states that I think a lot of people are really worried about in terms of battleground states, closely contested states where they cannot count the mail-in ballots
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我认为许多人真正感到担忧的州，就关键摇摆州、竞争激烈的州而言，在这些州，他们不能在选举日之前清点邮寄选票，

sentences.en: until Election Day.
sentences.zh: 直到选举日当天才能开始。

sentences.en: And Secretary of State Benson in Michigan has said repeatedly, it's not going to be Election
sentences.zh: 密歇根州务卿本森曾多次表示，在密歇根州，

sentences.en: Pennsylvania, likewise, also won't count ballots.

sentences.en: Until Election Day.

sentences.en: And they have some of the most contentious lawsuits in the country.
sentences.zh: 而且他们拥有全国最具争议的一些诉讼。

sentences.en: And as we talked about earlier, with the perhaps 100,000 ballots that could be thrown out.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前讨论过的，可能有高达10万张选票面临被废弃的风险。

sentences.en: So those two states in particular, I think, which could determine the election, we could be waiting for days and days in those states.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为尤其是这两个可能决定选举结果的州，我们在这些州可能需要等待好几天。

sentences.en: You know, when you use phrases like Election Week, it reminds me of a conversation we had with our colleague Reid Epstein a couple of weeks back about the pretty bruising,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你使用“选举周”这样的词组时，让我想起了几周前我们与同事里德·爱泼斯坦的一次谈话，谈到了全国各地围绕邮寄投票所经历的相当痛苦的初选过程。

sentences.en: primary experience that involved mail-in voting around the country.
sentences.zh: 初选过程。

sentences.en: And Reid's advice was, look, after election night, turn off your TV, take a mental vacation, check back in two weeks later.
sentences.zh: 里德的建议是：听着，选举之夜过后，关掉电视，让大脑度个假，两周后再来看看结果。

sentences.en: It's a waiting game.
sentences.zh: 这是一场耐心的游戏。

sentences.en: It will be frustrating, but ultimately, perhaps not the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 这会令人沮丧，但终究可能并非世界末日。

sentences.en: Well, I do think that's generally right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实认为这大致是正确的。

sentences.en: Like, I do think voters need to adjust their expectations for what a normal election night
sentences.zh: 比如，我确实认为选民需要调整对正常选举之夜样貌的预期，如果在选举之夜无法得知宾夕法尼亚州、密歇根州和威斯康星州的赢家，不得不等待两、三、四、五、六天，也不要惊慌失措。

sentences.en: will look like and not freak out if they don't know the winners of Pennsylvania and Michigan and Wisconsin on election night and they have to wait two, three, four, five, six days.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，对于关心民主的人来说，有一个更大的担忧。

sentences.en: But I do think there's a bigger concern for people who are concerned about democracy.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，清点这些邮寄选票的时间越长，某些州的竞争越白热化，你就会看到针对每一张选票的法律挑战越多。

sentences.en: And I do think that the longer it takes to get these mail-in ballots counted and the closer

sentences.en: it is in some states, the more you're going to have legal challenges to every single ballot.

sentences.en: I wonder why you're framing it that way.

sentences.en: Well, because of the partisan divide on mail-in voting, there's now a very strong incentive

sentences.en: for Democrats to fight for every mail-in ballot to count and Republicans to oppose every mail-in ballot that's sent in.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果你在一个民主党人的邮寄投票数是共和党人三倍的州里，

sentences.en: These arguments will often be done under the guides of election security and fraud prevention.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么共和党人希望确保任何能够被取消资格的邮寄选票都被取消资格，因为他们想要赢。

sentences.en: But generally, there's a huge partisan incentive to take these positions.
sentences.zh: 你也可以理解为什么民主党人希望确保每一张邮寄选票都被计算在内，因为他们也想赢。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you're in a state where it's three to one Democrats voting by mail over Republicans,

sentences.en: you can see why the Republicans want to make sure every mail-in ballot that can be disqualified is disqualified because they want to win.

sentences.en: Look, the question on everyone's mind is what happens during this waiting period and whether or not the president seeks to capitalize on the red mirage for as long as it may exiSt.

sentences.en: And I'm mindful that a couple of nights ago, both candidates were asked during the presidential

sentences.en: And the president did not commit to that.

sentences.en: the election, it's because of fraud or scams or cheating, as he said during the debate.

sentences.en: And so he can walk away with his head high that he's a winner and his supporters can feel like he's a winner.

sentences.zh: 如果是一场压倒性的胜利，我们就不会闲坐两三周，在宾夕法尼亚州最高法院为每一张最后的选票争论不休。
